hero.headline: Federal prosecutors directed to prioritize birth tourism cases after Supreme Court ruling
hero.body:
The Trump administration is shifting its strategy to target birth tourism following the Supreme Court's decision to uphold birthright citizenship. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche announced that federal prosecutors and law enforcement will focus on combating cases where tourists and temporary visitors travel to the United States specifically to give birth.

"There's other things that the Department of Homeland Security can do, and the federal government can do in the visa process and the application process, to try to minimize or limit the opportunity of folks coming here not to visit, and not to do what they're saying they're doing on the tourist visa, but just to have a baby that can then be a US citizen," Blanche told reporters.

The Department of Justice's assistant attorney general for the national fraud division issued an office-wide memo directing staff to bring fraud charges in alleged birth tourism cases. "The Department of Justice will zealously protect the sanctity of United States citizenship by investigating and prosecuting those who fraudulently exploit our immigration system," Colin McDonald wrote.

The administration had initially sought to use an executive order to redefine the Fourteenth Amendment's birthright citizenship protections, arguing that children born to non-citizen parents with temporary legal status or unlawful presence would not qualify for automatic citizenship. However, the Supreme Court rejected this approach in a 6-3 decision, with Chief Justice John Roberts writing that the administration provided "scant evidence for this dramatically revisionist view."

The focus on birth tourism represents a narrower legal strategy after the broader birthright citizenship challenge failed. During oral arguments in the case, the government's own lawyer acknowledged that "no one knows for sure" how significant birth tourism actually is. The Center for Immigration Studies, an anti-immigration organization, estimated there are between 20,000 to 26,000 births by women on tourist visas annually, representing less than 1 percent of all babies born in the United States each year.

Despite the relatively small numbers, Republican lawmakers have emphasized their concerns about the practice. House Speaker Mike Johnson stated that birth tourism has been "grossly abused in recent years," claiming that people come to the country to give birth so their children can access welfare benefits.

Vice President JD Vance also weighed in on the ruling, criticizing the Supreme Court's decision. "Do I think she made a mistake in the ruling? I do," Vance said, referring to Justice Amy Coney Barrett's vote to uphold birthright citizenship protections.

The administration is now pushing Congress to pass new legislation creating exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born to parents without permanent legal status. However, any such legislation would need to overcome the 60-vote filibuster threshold, which has proved difficult for divisive bills during the second Trump term.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran agree to continue nuclear discussions after Qatar meetings
cards.teaser: American and Iranian negotiators met separately with mediators in Qatar, with the host country reporting positive progress.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately on Wednesday with mediators from Qatar and Pakistan. Both sides agreed to continue their discussions, according to Qatar, which hosted the meetings.

The talks represent the latest round of diplomatic engagement between Washington and Tehran. Rather than meeting directly, American and Iranian officials each held separate sessions with the mediating teams.

cards.headline: Iran Prepares Funeral Ceremonies for Supreme Leader Killed in Strike
cards.teaser: Long-delayed funeral ceremonies for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei are set to begin Friday, six days after his death during strikes at the outset of conflict.
cards.body:
Iran will begin funeral ceremonies Friday for Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed during strikes by the United States and Israel at the beginning of the current conflict. The ceremonies have been delayed for six days and will take place across two countries over multiple days.

The funeral represents a significant moment for the Iranian government to demonstrate its stability and continuity after the loss of its highest leader. Officials view the ceremonies as an opportunity to show both domestic and international audiences that the regime has endured despite the leadership change.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall for third consecutive day after US-Iran talks conclude in Doha
cards.teaser: Oil prices extended their decline following the conclusion of negotiations between the United States and Iran in Doha.
cards.body:
Oil markets continued their losing streak on Thursday, with prices falling for the third consecutive day following the conclusion of US-Iran talks in Doha. The decline pushed Brent crude to its lowest levels since the US-Israel conflict with Iran began, marking its worst quarter since 2020.

The price drop reflects easing regional tensions and increased oil supply flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. As hopes for lasting peace grow, fuel costs that had surged during the height of conflict concerns are now plummeting, with diesel experiencing its biggest monthly fall in 26 years.

cards.headline: US and Iran Conclude Indirect Talks in Qatar
cards.teaser: Negotiations between American and Iranian representatives wrapped up in Doha with President Trump describing the meetings as productive.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators held separate meetings in Qatar on Wednesday, with Qatari and Pakistani mediators facilitating the discussions. Both sides agreed to continue their talks going forward. According to Qatar's statement, positive progress was made during the sessions.

President Trump described the meetings as very good, indicating satisfaction with how the negotiations unfolded. The talks addressed tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital waterway for global oil transportation.

cards.headline: China Enacts Ethnic Unity Law with Overseas Reach
cards.teaser: China has implemented a new ethnic unity law that extends its legal authority beyond its borders and mandates integration of ethnic minorities.
cards.body:
China's new ethnic unity law came into effect despite warnings from Taiwan, the United Nations, and human rights organizations. The law aims to create a shared national identity among ethnic groups, including strengthening Mandarin as the official language. Critics fear it will further erode the rights of Uyghurs, Tibetans, and other minorities that Beijing is accused of persecuting.

The law also extends China's legal reach overseas, raising concerns about Beijing's ability to pursue dissidents abroad. A bipartisan group of 14 House lawmakers, led by Representatives McGovern, Smith, and Khanna, called on the State Department to condemn the legislation. Three bipartisan congressional measures were introduced in response to the new legal framework.

cards.headline: European Union Sets October Deadline for China Trade Deficit Reduction
cards.teaser: The EU has given itself until October to reduce its trade deficit with China, though concerns about retaliation are complicating efforts.
cards.body:
The European Union and China have agreed to enter three months of formal trade consultations to address the bloc's €360 billion annual trade deficit. This marks their first joint statement in seven years and comes after weeks of threats and tensions between the two sides.

The talks aim to create a more balanced bilateral relationship and help the EU avoid a trade war with China. The agreement follows Chinese warnings of potential retaliation if the EU took measures to restrict the flow of Chinese goods and components into Europe.

hero.headline: Russia Launches Large-Scale Strikes on Kyiv, Killing at Least 13
hero.body:
Russia carried out its largest missile and drone attacks on Kyiv in weeks, killing at least 13 people and injuring scores more across the Ukrainian capital. Ukrainian officials reported a significant number of casualties, including children, as the strikes caused widespread damage throughout the city.

The attacks represented a major escalation in Russian bombardment of the capital after a relative lull in recent weeks. Multiple neighborhoods sustained damage as missiles and drones struck residential and infrastructure targets. Emergency services worked through the morning to search damaged buildings and treat the wounded.

The assault on Kyiv was part of a broader wave of strikes across Ukraine. Poland scrambled fighter jets in response to the attack, while Finland imposed temporary airspace restrictions as a precautionary measure. The coordinated nature of the strikes and their intensity marked a shift in Russia's tactical approach to targeting the Ukrainian capital.

Ukrainian air defense systems intercepted some of the incoming missiles and drones, but the scale of the attack overwhelmed defenses in several areas. Officials described the operation as one of the most intensive Russian aerial campaigns against Kyiv since the early months of the conflict. The strikes hit during morning hours when many residents were beginning their daily routines.

The attack comes as international diplomatic efforts continue on multiple fronts related to regional conflicts. Ukrainian authorities have launched investigations into the strikes and are assessing the full extent of damage to civilian infrastructure. Medical facilities across Kyiv received casualties throughout the morning, with hospitals reporting they were treating both serious and minor injuries from the bombardment.

cards.headline: Germany Charges Ukrainian National Over Nord Stream Pipeline Explosions
cards.teaser: German prosecutors have filed charges against a Ukrainian suspect in connection with the explosions that destroyed the Nord Stream gas pipelines.
cards.body:
German authorities have charged a Ukrainian national in connection with the September 2022 explosions that destroyed sections of the Nord Stream gas pipelines. This marks the first formal legal action in the investigation into the underwater blasts that severed the pipelines connecting Russia to Germany.

Ukraine has denied involvement in the case. The charges carry potential implications for Ukraine's relationship with Germany, as the Nord Stream pipelines had been a significant geopolitical issue before their destruction.

cards.headline: Fuel Shortages Worsen in Russia Amid Refinery Attacks
cards.teaser: Russian citizens face worsening gasoline shortages as Ukrainian drone strikes on oil refineries disrupt domestic fuel supplies.
cards.body:
Russia is experiencing a deepening fuel crisis as shortages spread across the country, prompting fights at gas stations and forcing the government to seek imports. Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries have disrupted domestic fuel production, creating supply problems during the summer months. President Vladimir Putin acknowledged the fuel shortages publicly.

Russia has turned to purchasing gasoline from India to address the shortages, according to sources familiar with the transactions. Videos showed confrontations breaking out at Russian gas stations as motorists competed for limited fuel supplies. The crisis marks a tangible impact of the conflict on Russian civilians and the domestic economy.

cards.headline: Trump Proposes Syrian Role in Hezbollah Containment
cards.teaser: President Trump suggested during peace talks that Syria could help subdue Hezbollah in Lebanon, a proposal that has confused regional observers.
cards.body:
President Trump repeatedly raised the possibility during peace negotiations that Syria could assist in containing Hezbollah forces in Lebanon. The proposal emerged during diplomatic talks focused on regional stability but has left many observers in the Middle East uncertain about its feasibility or intent.

The suggestion revived difficult historical memories in the region, where Syrian and Lebanese relations have been strained by decades of conflict and occupation. Syria and Hezbollah have been aligned for years, making Trump's proposal particularly unexpected to regional analysts and diplomats familiar with Middle Eastern alliances.

cards.headline: New York officials urge residents to set thermostats to 78 degrees during heat wave
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani activated the city's heat emergency plan as dangerous temperatures hit New York City and the broader tri-state area.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faced criticism after urging residents to set their air conditioners to 78 degrees during a blistering heat wave affecting the region. The mayor activated the city's heat emergency plan as dangerous temperatures struck the city and surrounding areas.

The recommendation drew backlash from residents enduring the extreme heat. Public facilities also faced scrutiny, with Red Hook's public pool remaining closed despite the dangerous conditions. Cooling centers opened across neighborhoods including the Upper West Side to provide relief for residents without adequate air conditioning.

cards.headline: World Cup fans say tickets bought on StubHub canceled at last minute
cards.teaser: Hundreds of fans who purchased World Cup tickets through resale site StubHub report having their tickets canceled shortly before matches.
cards.body:
Hundreds of World Cup fans who purchased tickets through resale platform StubHub have reported having their tickets cancelled at the last minute. The cancellations left attendees unable to enter stadiums despite having confirmed purchases, forcing many to miss matches they had paid for.

The incident affected fans who had made significant financial commitments for their World Cup trips. One attendee reported spending $6,000 on travel and accommodations based on a ticket purchase that ultimately failed to work at the stadium gate.

cards.headline: Trump financial disclosure shows wealth increased during presidency
cards.teaser: President Trump's wealth grew at a scale without modern presidential precedent, according to newly released financial disclosures.
cards.body:
President Trump's financial disclosures reveal he earned more than $2 billion last year, with over $1 billion coming from cryptocurrency ventures. The earnings represent an unprecedented level of wealth accumulation during a modern presidency.

The crypto gains raise questions about potential conflicts of interest, as Trump has actively pushed to deregulate the cryptocurrency industry while simultaneously profiting substantially from it. The financial documents provide details on his holdings and business activities during his time in office.

cards.headline: Russian missile and drone strikes kill at least 13 in Kyiv
cards.teaser: Russia launched its largest strikes on the Ukrainian capital in weeks, with ballistic and cruise missiles damaging buildings across the city.
cards.body:
Russia launched its largest missile and drone assault on Kyiv in weeks, killing at least 13 people and injuring 86 others, with children among the casualties. The overnight strikes hit multiple districts across the capital, damaging residential buildings and a hotel on one of Kyiv's central boulevards. Fires burned at various sites as emergency crews responded to the widespread damage to civilian infrastructure.

The attack employed ballistic and cruise missiles alongside drones. Local authorities warned the death toll could rise as emergency services continued their response. The strikes came as Russia faces fuel shortages following Ukrainian long-range attacks on Russian oil refineries.

cards.headline: U.S. and Iran agree to continue nuclear discussions after Qatar meetings
cards.teaser: American and Iranian negotiators met separately with mediators in Qatar, with the host country reporting positive progress.
cards.body:
U.S. and Iranian negotiators met separately on Wednesday with mediators from Qatar and Pakistan. Both sides agreed to continue their discussions, according to Qatar, which hosted the meetings.

The talks represent the latest round of diplomatic engagement between Washington and Tehran. Rather than meeting directly, American and Iranian officials each held separate sessions with the mediating teams.

cards.headline: Convicted people smuggler found working illegally in UK while seeking asylum
cards.teaser: A people smuggler previously convicted in France has been located by the BBC living in Leicestershire and working illegally.
cards.body:
A man once known as the "godfather" of French migrant camps has been discovered living in Leicestershire and working illegally while pursuing an asylum claim in the UK. The BBC located and confronted the individual, who had previously been convicted of people smuggling offenses in France.

The BBC investigation revealed that despite his criminal history, he entered the UK and submitted an asylum application. He was found working in a Leicestershire village while his case was being processed.

hero.headline: South Korean stocks tumble 6% as chipmakers hit by AI selloff
hero.body:
South Korean stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Thursday, with the main index dropping 6% as chipmakers faced losses in a global retreat from artificial intelligence-related investments. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, two of the world's largest memory chip producers, saw their shares fall more than 7% during the trading session.

The Seoul market weakness followed declines on Wall Street, where technology stocks had pulled major indexes lower. Investor sentiment has shifted as concerns grew about whether valuations in the AI sector have become stretched. This apprehension triggered a broad pullback from semiconductor stocks that have performed strongly over the past year due to surging demand for AI hardware.

The selloff rippled across Asian markets on Thursday, with chipmakers bearing the largest losses. Stock futures in the United States also signaled further potential weakness ahead, suggesting that volatility in technology shares could persist as traders awaited key employment data scheduled for later in the day.

South Korean chipmakers have been among the biggest winners from the AI boom, with Samsung and SK Hynix supplying high-bandwidth memory chips essential for data centers and AI training systems. The sharp decline in their stock prices marks a significant reversal from the robust gains these companies had achieved earlier in the year.

The broader regional market response highlighted growing skepticism about whether the recent AI-driven rallies have pushed stock valuations beyond sustainable levels. Technology investors across Asia retreated from their positions, with the movement spreading outward from initial Wall Street losses through exchanges in Japan, South Korea, and other major regional markets.

The timing of the selloff reflects multiple pressures on investor confidence. Market participants have grown increasingly cautious about whether the current levels of AI-related stock valuations can be justified. Additionally, concerns about potential interest rate increases from the Federal Reserve have added to the uncertainty weighing on technology stocks globally.

The losses represent a stark contrast to the enthusiasm that characterized the technology sector in earlier months. Companies whose valuations are heavily tied to artificial intelligence developments have faced particular pressure as investors reassess risk and potential returns in the sector.

The volatility underscores the sensitivity of markets to shifting sentiment around emerging technologies. Semiconductor companies, which sit at the center of AI infrastructure development, have become key indicators of investor confidence in the broader AI investment thesis. As traders worldwide reassess their positions, the movements in South Korean chipmaker stocks serve as a barometer for the health of global technology investments and the sustainability of valuations that have grown rapidly since AI applications gained widespread attention.

cards.teaser: Oil prices extended their decline following the conclusion of negotiations between the United States and Iran in Doha.
cards.body:
Oil markets continued their losing streak on Thursday, with prices falling for the third consecutive day following the conclusion of US-Iran talks in Doha. The decline pushed Brent crude to its lowest levels since the US-Israel conflict with Iran began, marking its worst quarter since 2020.

The price drop reflects easing regional tensions and increased oil supply flowing through the Strait of Hormuz. As hopes for lasting peace grow, fuel costs that had surged during the height of conflict concerns are now plummeting, with diesel experiencing its biggest monthly fall in 26 years.

cards.headline: US electrical grid faces emergency as heat wave strains power systems
cards.teaser: A widespread heat wave pushed the nation's largest power grid to emergency status as demand reached record levels.
cards.body:
The operator of the largest electrical grid in the United States issued an emergency alert as a heat wave stretched power systems to their limits. PJM Interconnection, which manages electricity for 13 states and the District of Columbia, reported record demand and significant price spikes as temperatures climbed.

The strain on the grid has been intensified by the growing number of data centers in the region, which consume large amounts of electricity for cooling and operations. More frequent heat waves are taxing power systems nationwide, increasing both demand and concerns about grid reliability during extreme weather events.

cards.headline: Japan shifts to surprise intervention tactics to support weakening yen
cards.teaser: Japanese authorities have adopted new tactics to combat currency speculators as the yen hits a 40-year low.
cards.body:
Japan has changed its approach to defending the yen, shifting to surprise intervention tactics aimed at catching short sellers off guard, according to sources familiar with the matter. The move comes as the Japanese currency has fallen to its weakest level against the dollar in four decades, prompting concern in Tokyo about the economic effects of the decline.

The government has already spent approximately $74 billion attempting to support the yen's value. Investors say the real challenge for Japanese authorities is the policy divergence with the Federal Reserve, which has kept interest rates higher than Japan's ultra-low rates. Traders are now considering worst-case scenarios for further yen declines if the currency crisis deepens.

cards.headline: Stock futures decline ahead of jobs report following weak July start
cards.teaser: US stock futures pointed lower as investors prepared for the release of employment data after markets stumbled early in July.
cards.body:
Stock futures fell on Thursday morning as traders awaited the release of the monthly jobs report, following a weak start to July trading. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq futures all wavered ahead of the employment data, which could influence Federal Reserve policy decisions.

Wall Street ended the previous session lower, with technology shares leading the decline and pulling major indexes down despite gains in most other stocks. The global selloff in artificial intelligence-related stocks has contributed to the choppy trading conditions as investors reassess valuations in the sector.

cards.headline: SEC investigates alleged insider trading scheme that cost Susquehanna $100 million
cards.teaser: Federal regulators are examining claims that insiders made substantial profits on trades related to a Chinese brokerage crackdown.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has opened an investigation into alleged insider trading that resulted in approximately $100 million in losses for trading firm Susquehanna. The probe centers on trades made ahead of a crackdown on Chinese brokerage operations, with insiders allegedly profiting from advance knowledge of regulatory actions.

Susquehanna won a court order to freeze accounts and subpoena brokers as part of its effort to identify those involved in the alleged scheme. The trading firm claims the insider trades were executed in a coordinated manner ahead of public announcements that moved markets, allowing the perpetrators to profit at Susquehanna's expense.

cards.headline: Singapore authorities seize $42 million mansion in Nvidia chip smuggling investigation
cards.teaser: A luxury home in Singapore was confiscated as part of a probe into illegal trade of AI semiconductor servers.
cards.body:
Singapore authorities have seized a $42 million luxury mansion as part of an investigation into the illegal trade of servers containing Nvidia AI semiconductors. The property confiscation is connected to smuggling operations targeting advanced chips that are subject to export controls.

The seizure highlights growing enforcement efforts against unauthorized movements of artificial intelligence technology. Nvidia's high-demand processors have become targets for underground smuggling networks attempting to bypass trade restrictions across multiple jurisdictions.

hero.headline: Scientists build first fully synthetic cell capable of complete life cycle
hero.body:
Researchers have created the first synthetic cell built entirely from laboratory components that can feed, grow, and reproduce, marking a significant milestone in bioengineering. The achievement represents a fundamental shift in how scientists approach building cellular life.

The synthetic cells, nicknamed SpudCells, differ fundamentally from previous efforts that modified existing organisms. Earlier projects, including efforts to create minimal bacterial genomes, still relied on inserting synthetic DNA into existing cellular machinery. This new work was built from the ground up to ensure every component was known and understood.

Dr. Kate Adamala, who led the research at the University of Minnesota, explained the rationale: "If we want to be able to engineer biology, we really have to understand exactly the blueprint, every component of it, so we know what we're changing."

SpudCells are tiny, water-filled spheres called liposomes, just a few thousandths of a millimetre wide, containing synthetic DNA and other essential components. The cells demonstrate the complete cycle of growth, genetic replication, and division to produce offspring. Adamala named them SpudCells to evoke Sputnik and the space age, but also acknowledged a personal connection: "I'm Polish. I'm mostly made of potatoes."

The synthetic cells function in a specially prepared liquid brimming with vital chemicals, including ATP, the main energy-carrying molecule that natural cells manufacture from nutrients. To grow, SpudCells fuse with tiny "feeder" liposomes containing molecules, enzymes, and ribosomes needed to make proteins. The SpudCell genome carries instructions to copy itself and divide. Researchers demonstrated how SpudCells with genetic advantages spread through populations, outcompeting original variants.

However, SpudCells remain far from being true living organisms. They are completely dependent on the substances in their surrounding liquid and cannot build their own protein-making machinery, control their metabolism, or clear waste. When they divide, they often pass on incorrect amounts of DNA and typically fail after a few generations.

Professor Tom Ellis from Imperial College London called the work probably the field's "biggest breakthrough in recent times." The achievement helps scientists understand the minimum requirements for life and how it might have emerged from chemistry, while also providing a fully understood system for testing biological models.

Adamala and others are now launching an institution called Biotic to develop SpudCells further. The goal is to build "an operating system for life" made from genes and biochemistry. While the cells could eventually be designed to produce drugs, foods, fuels, and other materials, significant work remains before they become practical for real-world applications.

The research was released as a preprint, allowing other laboratories to scrutinize the work before formal peer review.

cards.headline: NASA launches mission to rescue falling Swift space telescope
cards.teaser: The space agency is conducting a rescue operation to reposition a telescope sinking into Earth's atmosphere before it burns up.
cards.body:
NASA launched a mission on July 2 to save the Swift space telescope from burning up as it falls toward Earth. The telescope has been sinking into the atmosphere, requiring intervention to push it back into a stable orbit.

The Swift Boost mission represents an attempt to extend the operational life of the space telescope through a rendezvous in orbit. The rescue operation involves meeting the telescope in space and using propulsion to raise it to a higher altitude where atmospheric drag will not continue pulling it downward. The mission serves both scientific and defense purposes, according to NASA and other agencies monitoring the effort.

cards.headline: ULA launches 29 Amazon satellites on final Atlas V rocket
cards.teaser: An Atlas V rocket lifted off from Florida carrying satellites for Amazon's Leo broadband internet constellation.
cards.body:
United Launch Alliance launched 29 Amazon Leo broadband satellites to orbit from Cape Canaveral, Florida on July 2. The mission marked the final Atlas V rocket launch supporting Amazon's satellite internet constellation.

The launch was part of Amazon's effort to build a broadband internet network using low Earth orbit satellites. After liftoff from Cape Canaveral, the rocket may have been visible from areas including Tallahassee. The July launch schedule from Cape Canaveral includes multiple missions as commercial space activity continues to expand from Florida's Space Coast.

cards.headline: Researchers find planet that survived its star's death
cards.teaser: Scientists using the Webb telescope discovered a planet that endured when its star became a white dwarf, then migrated inward.
cards.body:
Scientists reported finding aerosols and hydrocarbons in the atmosphere of a planet orbiting a white dwarf star, evidence that the planet survived the death of its host star. The discovery, published in Nature, shows how some planets can endure the violent transformation when their star exhausts its fuel and collapses.

The Webb Space Telescope observations revealed that after surviving the star's death, the giant planet migrated inward toward the white dwarf. The findings suggest Earth's fate may depend on a delicate balance when the sun eventually dies. The research provides new data on how planetary systems evolve after their stars reach the end of their lives, a process that will eventually affect our own solar system.

cards.headline: Apple orders 10 million units of foldable iPhone Ultra
cards.teaser: The company placed manufacturing orders for a foldable iPhone model that could sell for around $2,500.
cards.body:
Apple has ordered 10 million units of a foldable iPhone Ultra model from its manufacturing partners, according to supply chain reports. The device could carry a price tag of approximately $2,500, positioning it as Apple's most expensive iPhone.

The foldable iPhone represents Apple's entry into a market already occupied by Samsung and other manufacturers. Reports suggest the iPhone 18 Pro series and the foldable iPhone Ultra could debut on September 8. The Ultra model would compete directly with devices like Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8 Wide as Apple brings its first foldable smartphone to market after years of development.

cards.headline: Italian tech company Bending Spoons surges 40% on first trading day
cards.teaser: The company, which has acquired brands including AOL, Evernote, and Vimeo, defied the SaaS market downturn with a strong IPO.
cards.body:
Bending Spoons jumped 40% on its first day of trading following an $18 billion initial public offering. The Italian company has built its portfolio by acquiring and revamping struggling technology brands including AOL, Eventbrite, Evernote, Meetup, and Vimeo.

The strong debut defied a broader slump affecting software-as-a-service stocks. According to the company's co-founders, their success stems from minimizing luck and learning from past failures, including setbacks from their own earlier startup ventures.

cards.headline: Apple plans new iPad Pro and MacBook Pro releases for early 2027
cards.teaser: The company is preparing several new iPad Pro tablets and a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro for release next year.
cards.body:
Apple is developing a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro and multiple new iPad Pro models for launch in the first half of 2027, according to Bloomberg. The MacBook Pro refresh will mark a significant update to the company's budget-friendly laptop offering.

Apple is testing four new iPad Pro variants scheduled for spring 2027, focusing on internal improvements. The company is also working on M6-equipped MacBook Pro models for late 2026, with an M7 version following in the first half of 2027 as part of its broader professional computing lineup refresh.

hero.headline: Celtics trade Jaylen Brown to 76ers for Paul George and draft picks
hero.body:
The Boston Celtics have completed a major trade, sending 2024 NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for forward Paul George and significant draft capital, according to multiple reports.

Boston will receive Paul George along with two first-round picks and two second-round picks as part of the deal. The trade comes after what has been described as a stormy few weeks, during which Brown expressed unhappiness with his treatment by the Celtics organization.

Brown has been a cornerstone of the Celtics since entering the league and just finished a season in which he was named the NBA Finals MVP. His departure marks a major shift in Boston's roster construction and represents a significant moment for the franchise.

In acquiring Brown, Philadelphia is making a bold move to strengthen its championship contention in the Eastern Conference. The 76ers are betting that adding a younger star player will elevate their competitive standing and help them build a roster capable of winning at the highest level. Brown's combination of scoring ability and defensive prowess makes him a valuable addition to any team.

For the Celtics, the trade brings in George, an experienced All-Star with multiple selections to the prestigious team. George has established himself as an elite two-way player during stints with the Indiana Pacers and the Los Angeles Clippers. His arrival provides Boston with veteran leadership and proven performance at the championship level.

The draft picks included in the deal give the Celtics flexibility for future roster moves. Boston can use the assets to develop young talent or package them together for additional trades as the organization moves forward.

The trade signals a new direction for both franchises as they enter critical phases of their competitive windows. For Philadelphia, the focus will be on how effectively Brown integrates with the existing core and whether he can deliver the impact needed to advance their championship aspirations. Boston must determine if George can maintain his elite performance level while fitting into the team's system.

Both players will face pressure to justify the magnitude of this swap. Brown will need to prove he can elevate Philadelphia's performance, while George must demonstrate he remains a difference-maker at the highest level of competition. The draft picks acquired by Boston could prove to be valuable assets if the organization uses them strategically in the years ahead.

This blockbuster trade is among the most significant moves of the offseason and will be closely monitored as both teams prepare for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: US advances to World Cup Round of 16 with 2-0 win over Bosnia-Herzegovina
cards.teaser: The United States defeated Bosnia-Herzegovina 2-0 in Santa Clara to secure passage to the World Cup knockout stage.
cards.body:
The United States defeated Bosnia-Herzegovina 2-0 to secure passage to the World Cup Round of 16. Folarin Balogun scored the opening goal, his third of the tournament, putting the US in control at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium.

The victory was marred when Balogun received a straight red card roughly 20 minutes after his goal for contact with Bosnia-Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemović. The dismissal sparked debate over the severity of the decision, with reports suggesting VAR protocols may have been misapplied. US Soccer cannot appeal the suspension, meaning Balogun will miss the upcoming Round of 16 matchup against Belgium.

cards.headline: Charlie Dean guides England to World Cup semifinal as stand-in captain
cards.teaser: England's Charlie Dean has led her team to the World Cup semifinals while serving as stand-in captain.
cards.body:
Charlie Dean has led England to the Women's World Cup semifinals as stand-in captain, turning around what could have been a career-defining moment after a crushing dismissal at Lord's. Her composed leadership has provided stability for the team through the tournament's knockout stages.

Dean's calm approach has guided England through challenging matches on their path to the semifinals, demonstrating her capability to handle pressure in the role.

cards.headline: US to face Belgium in World Cup Round of 16 in Seattle
cards.teaser: The United States will meet Belgium in Seattle for their World Cup Round of 16 matchup.
cards.body:
The United States men's team will return to Seahawks stadium in Seattle for their World Cup Round of 16 fixture against Belgium. The match represents a crucial test as the Americans seek to reach the quarterfinals.

Oddsmakers have listed the United States and Belgium matchup as a toss-up, with neither team holding a clear advantage. The game will determine which side advances to the World Cup quarterfinals.

cards.headline: Lando Norris says he is paying the price for his 2025 championship effort
cards.teaser: Formula 1 champion Lando Norris told BBC Sport he is dealing with the aftermath of his title-winning season.

Original card text retained

cards.headline: Wales makes six changes for Nations Championship opener against Fiji
cards.teaser: Wales head coach Steve Tandy has altered his lineup for the team's first match in the Nations Championship.
cards.body:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy has made six changes to the squad for the Nations Championship opener against Fiji. Louis Rees-Zammit returns to the wing position after Wales's recent victory over the Barbarians.

The alterations reflect Tandy's selection strategy as Wales kicks off their Nations Championship campaign with the changes made from the side that defeated the Barbarians.

cards.headline: Four British players remain in Wimbledon singles competition
cards.teaser: Britain has four players still competing in the singles draws at this year's Wimbledon tournament.
cards.body:
In her first BBC Sport column covering this year's Wimbledon, Naomi Broady examines whether Britain's final four singles players can help shift the mood surrounding the home Grand Slam.

The quartet's continued presence in the tournament offers an opportunity to lift the gloom that has surrounded British performances earlier in the championship.

hero.headline: Madonna releases Confessions II, first studio album in four years
hero.body:
Madonna has released Confessions II, her 15th studio album and first in four years, arriving 21 years after the original Confessions on a Dance Floor. The album debuted Thursday following a livestream preview for fans.

The new record draws inspiration from Madonna's 2023 Celebration tour, which revisited her back catalogue through recreated music videos. That experience prompted reflection on her past, evident throughout Confessions II's numerous references to her career. The album mirrors its predecessor's structure, opening with house-influenced tracks that flow together like a DJ mix before transitioning to slower, more introspective material reminiscent of her 1998 album Bedtime Stories.

The production, handled by Stuart Price and others including Andrew Watt and Cirkut, relies on established dance music styles rather than cutting-edge trends. Influences range from Chicago house music classics to 1990s trip-hop, with touches of UK garage and Euro pop-dance. Standout tracks include Danceteria, which vividly recalls her early 1980s New York club scene with references to artists Jean-Michel Basquiat and Keith Haring, and Fragile, an acoustic-driven tribute to her late brother Christopher.

The lyrics reveal vulnerability and reflection. Songs like The Test, a duet with her daughter Lourdes, explore maternal regret, while LES Girl recounts a relationship with an ambitious bohemian ex. The album balances standard Madonna confidence with brittle, regretful moments that showcase her willingness to be emotionally open.

Reviews have highlighted the album's cohesive sound and confidence, with critics describing it as a hypnotic dancefloor experience. One reviewer called it "a sweaty dance party" positioning Madonna to reclaim her place in pop music. However, some critics note the album runs nearly ten minutes longer than the original without needing the extra length, suggesting a few house tracks could have been trimmed.

While Confessions II lacks an obvious pop smash single comparable to Hung Up from the original album, Danceteria comes close with its bright disco-house production. Critics agree the record represents Madonna's strongest work since the original Confessions on a Dance Floor, which sold 10 million copies worldwide and remains her last unqualified commercial triumph. Her subsequent albums have each sold roughly half what their predecessors did, with 2019's Madame X shifting 500,000 copies.

The album arrives as Madonna, now in her late 60s, navigates a transformed pop landscape. TikTok launched a multi-part global campaign supporting the release, reflecting modern music promotion strategies. For fans who followed Madonna through the 1980s and 1990s, Confessions II appears to offer the reconnection they've been awaiting.

cards.headline: The Onion's Infowars parody launches with $100,000 payment to Sandy Hook families
cards.teaser: The satirical news site has relaunched the conspiracy website as a comedic project, beginning with a six-figure donation to families affected by the 2012 shooting.
cards.body:
The Onion launched its parody version of Infowars this week, starting the project with a $100,000 payment to families of Sandy Hook shooting victims. The satirical publication acquired the right-wing conspiracy website after its founder Alex Jones lost a defamation lawsuit to the families. Comedian Tim Heidecker is participating in the relaunch.

The Washington Post described the project as a comedic revenge story, while Variety reported that the relaunch is proceeding even amid legal questions about whether The Onion can legally operate the site. Jones had spread false claims that the 2012 Sandy Hook Elementary School shooting was staged, leading to a multi-million dollar judgment against him. The Onion's version of the site will send money to the families who won the defamation case.

cards.headline: Lil Wayne apologizes for missing his own concert in Maine
cards.teaser: The rapper failed to appear at a stop on his 20 Years of Carter Classics tour and issued an apology to fans.
cards.body:
Lil Wayne did not show up for his scheduled concert in Maine as part of his 20 Years of Carter Classics tour. The rapper later apologized to fans who had attended the show expecting to see him perform.

Lil Wayne posted an apology saying he was sorry for the absence. The tour celebrates two decades since his Carter album series began, which has been central to his career and influence in hip-hop. No explanation was provided for why he missed the Maine performance.

cards.headline: Josh Gad joins Margot Robbie and Bradley Cooper in Ocean's prequel
cards.teaser: The actor has signed on for a significant role in the period heist film set before the events of Ocean's 11.
cards.body:
Josh Gad will appear in the upcoming Ocean's 11 prequel alongside Margot Robbie and Bradley Cooper, according to Warner Bros. sources. Gad has booked what is described as a significant role in the period heist film. Monica Barbaro is also in talks to join the cast.

Cooper is directing and starring in the film, which is set before the events of the 2001 Ocean's 11 remake. Casting for the ensemble film has been ongoing, with multiple actors joining the project in recent weeks. The Ocean's franchise has produced several sequels and spinoffs since Steven Soderbergh's 2001 film revived the property.

cards.headline: Cardi B wins $60,000 from blogger Tasha K over social media posts
cards.teaser: A court ruled the blogger violated a previous agreement stemming from Cardi B's 2022 defamation victory.
cards.body:
Cardi B was awarded $60,000 from blogger Tasha K over posts about the rapper's husband Offset and NFL player Stefon Diggs. The ruling found that Tasha K violated terms of a deal that followed Cardi B's $4 million defamation victory against the blogger in 2022.

The original 2022 case resulted in a multi-million dollar judgment in Cardi B's favor after Tasha K made false claims about the rapper. The new award relates to posts made after that initial judgment and settlement agreement. The case adds to ongoing legal disputes between the rapper and the blogger.

cards.headline: Academy's chief Oscars officer transitions to consultant role
cards.teaser: Teni Melidonian is stepping down as awards production moves under new leadership ahead of the ceremony's planned move to YouTube in 2029.
cards.body:
Teni Melidonian, the Academy's chief Oscars officer, is leaving her position and will continue as a consultant for the next year. Academy CEO Bill Kramer informed staff of the transition in an email. Awards production will now fall under Jennifer Davidson's oversight.

Melidonian served as the primary liaison between the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and Disney/ABC. Her departure comes as the Oscars ceremony prepares for a major shift, with the broadcast set to move to YouTube in 2029. The change in leadership marks a significant transition period for the Academy's flagship awards show.

cards.headline: Indian filmmaker Nagraj Manjule announces release date for wrestling biopic
cards.teaser: The Marathi-language film tells the story of Olympic wrestler Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav and marks Manjule's return to regional cinema.
cards.body:
Jio Studios and Aatpat Productions unveiled a teaser and worldwide release date for Khashaba, a biographical sports drama about Indian Olympic wrestler Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav. The film is directed by Nagraj Manjule in the Marathi language.

Manjule previously won an Indian National Film Award for his 2013 film Fandry and directed the 2016 hit Sairat. Khashaba represents his return to Marathi-language filmmaking after those earlier regional successes. The film will receive a worldwide theatrical release from Jio Studios.

hero.headline: House meltdown signals legislative standstill through summer
hero.teaser: Recent dysfunction in the House of Representatives suggests major lawmaking may be finished for the 119th Congress.
hero.body:
Congress appears headed for an inactive summer session following recent breakdowns in House proceedings. The House experienced what observers described as a meltdown this week, adding to signs that substantive legislation is unlikely to advance during the remainder of the current congressional session.

The 119th Congress has struggled to pass major bills despite unified party control. Legislative activity has slowed as members prepare for the approaching midterm election cycle, with attention shifting from policymaking to campaign concerns.

cards.headline: Trump flies on new Air Force One gifted by Qatar
cards.teaser: President Trump took his first flight on a new Air Force One aircraft yesterday, a Boeing 747 luxury jet given to the United States by the government of Qatar.
cards.body:
President Trump took his first flight on a new Air Force One aircraft yesterday, a Boeing 747 luxury jet given to the United States by the government of Qatar. The gift has raised questions about ethics and security protocols surrounding the presidential aircraft.

The acceptance of a foreign government's gift for use as the official presidential aircraft marks a departure from traditional procurement processes. Air Force One aircraft have historically been purchased and maintained by the U.S. government through standard federal acquisition channels. The Boeing 747 luxury jet will now serve as the primary aircraft for presidential travel.

Concerns have emerged about whether the Qatari-provided aircraft has undergone the full range of security and maintenance checks typically required for Air Force One. Presidential aircraft must meet stringent standards for communications systems, defensive capabilities, and mechanical reliability. The security vetting process for Air Force One typically involves extensive testing and modification by U.S. military and intelligence agencies.

The ethics questions center on the appropriateness of accepting such a significant gift from a foreign government. Qatar maintains close diplomatic and military ties with the United States, hosting a major U.S. military base, but the acceptance of expensive gifts from foreign powers typically requires careful review under federal ethics laws. The White House has not publicly addressed the ethics review process or security certification procedures that were followed before the president's flight.

The new aircraft represents a significant upgrade in presidential travel capabilities. Boeing 747s are among the largest commercial aircraft in operation and can be extensively modified for presidential use. Previous Air Force One aircraft have been highly customized Boeing 747-200B models that served multiple administrations over decades of service.

cards.headline: Democratic Socialists gaining ground ahead of midterm elections
cards.teaser: A series of primary victories by Democratic Socialist candidates is creating strategic challenges for the Democratic Party.
cards.body:
Democratic Socialist candidates have secured notable primary victories across multiple states, including New York and Colorado. The Democratic Socialists of America have expanded their presence in government, with members now serving in Congress and holding mayoral positions in major cities.

The movement's growing influence reflects increased membership and shifting priorities within activist circles, including heightened focus on issues like Palestinian activism. Party leadership must now navigate how to integrate these candidates into their midterm strategy as they work to regain a congressional majority.

cards.headline: Trump pushes for mail voting restrictions in SAVE America Act
cards.teaser: The president is pressing Congress to include mail voting limitations that face opposition within his own party.
cards.body:
A federal judge has blocked a proposed restriction on mail-in voting, marking the second court setback for Trump's plan to limit mail ballots across the US. US District Judge Emmet Sullivan ruled against a US Postal Service plan that would have denied ballots to voters in states refusing to turn over their voter rolls to the federal government.

The push for mail voting restrictions has created tension within the Republican caucus. Some GOP lawmakers have expressed concern about supporting voting restrictions that could face public backlash in their districts.

cards.headline: Kelly backs ousted admiral running for South Carolina House seat
cards.teaser: Senator Mark Kelly endorsed Nancy Lacore, a three-star admiral fired by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, for Congress.
cards.body:
Sen. Mark Kelly of Arizona endorsed Democrat Nancy Lacore for South Carolina's 1st Congressional District on Wednesday. Lacore, who served as the 16th Chief of Navy Reserve, was fired without cause by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth last year.

Lacore is seeking to replace Rep. Nancy Mace in the House. If elected, she would bring three decades of naval service to Congress. Kelly's endorsement adds national profile to a race in a district that has been represented by Republicans.

cards.headline: New York City mayor to mark America's 250th anniversary with speech
cards.teaser: Mayor Zohran Mamdani plans to deliver a speech on Friday celebrating the nation's 250th birthday alongside newly naturalized citizens.
cards.body:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is scheduled to give a speech marking America's 250th birthday on Friday. The mayor, who was born in Uganda and later became a U.S. citizen, will be joined by recently naturalized citizens during the address.

Mamdani's speech is planned for hours before President Trump delivers his own address to the nation. The scheduling places the Democratic mayor's message in direct temporal proximity to the president's remarks on the anniversary.

cards.headline: Illinois governor accuses Trump of having dementia
cards.teaser: Gov. JB Pritzker said President Trump is suffering from dementia after recent presidential statements.
cards.body:
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker accused President Trump of suffering from dementia during a CNN interview on Tuesday. Anchor Kaitlan Collins asked Pritzker about recent comments by the president, including a claim that communism represents a bigger threat to the United States than both world wars, the Pearl Harbor attack, and the September 11 attacks combined.

Pritzker made the assessment while discussing Trump's fitness for office. The governor did not provide medical evidence to support the claim. Such accusations between political opponents are not uncommon, though they typically lack clinical backing.
